title: The Fibre That Prefers a Caress

scenes.tts: Brush a forearm slowly, then at a caress, then fast. One touch fibre seems to care how fast you stroke. Could that be why a caress feels nice?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Fibre That Prefers a Caress. A soft brush poised over the hairy skin of a forearm. Question on screen: does a fibre that prefers a speed explain the caress?
scenes.narration: Brush a forearm slowly, then at a caress, then fast. One touch fibre seems to care how fast you stroke. Could that be why a caress feels nice?

scenes.tts: Put the speeds in your hand. Mark a ten centimetre path on the forearm.
scenes.caption: Put the speeds in your hand. Mark a 10 cm path on the forearm.
scenes.visual: A forearm with a 10 cm path marked by two dots and a ruler.
scenes.narration: Put the speeds in your hand. Mark a 10 cm path on the forearm.

scenes.tts: At three centimetres per second, a brush crosses it in about three seconds: a slow caress.
scenes.caption: At 3 cm/s, a brush crosses it in about 3 seconds: a slow caress.
scenes.visual: The brush crosses the path; an on-screen timer stops at 3.3 s. Label: 3 cm/s, a slow caress.
scenes.narration: At 3 cm/s, a brush crosses it in about 3 seconds: a slow caress.

scenes.tts: Ten times faster is a quick swipe. Ten times slower is a crawl of over half a minute.
scenes.visual: Two more runs: 30 cm/s, timer 0.33 s, label quick swipe; 0.3 cm/s, time-lapsed and labelled so, timer 33 s, label crawl.
scenes.narration: Ten times faster is a quick swipe. Ten times slower is a crawl of over half a minute.

scenes.tts: A low-threshold mechanoreceptor responds to gentle force. Hairy skin has fast, myelinated ones and slow, unmyelinated ones.
scenes.visual: Term card: low-threshold mechanoreceptor (LTMR) = a sensory neuron that responds to gentle mechanical force.
scenes.narration: A low-threshold mechanoreceptor responds to gentle force. Hairy skin has fast, myelinated ones and slow, unmyelinated ones.

scenes.tts: A C-tactile afferent is a human one with a thin, unmyelinated axon. It conducts slowly.
scenes.visual: Beside it, a thin bare axon; a spike creeps along it. Label: C-tactile (CT) afferent, unmyelinated, slow.
scenes.narration: A C-tactile afferent is a human one with a thin, unmyelinated axon. It conducts slowly.

scenes.tts: Microneurography records single axons from a skin nerve in an awake person.
scenes.visual: Schematic: a fine electrode passes through the skin into a peripheral nerve of the arm; a spike raster builds in real time. Label: microneurography.
scenes.narration: Microneurography records single axons from a skin nerve in an awake person.

scenes.tts: In two thousand nine, Loken and colleagues recorded this way while a soft brush crossed the forearm at set speeds.
scenes.caption: In 2009, Löken and colleagues recorded this way while a soft brush crossed the forearm at set speeds.
scenes.visual: A brush crosses one fibre's receptive field on the forearm while the raster builds. Label: Löken, Wessberg, Morrison, McGlone and Olausson, 2009.
scenes.narration: In 2009, Löken and colleagues recorded this way while a soft brush crossed the forearm at set speeds.

scenes.tts: The recorded myelinated touch fibres fired harder the faster the brush moved.
scenes.visual: A logarithmic velocity axis appears. The myelinated curve draws in, rising steadily from slow to fast. Label: myelinated afferents recorded.
scenes.narration: The recorded myelinated touch fibres fired harder the faster the brush moved.

scenes.tts: Predict. If C-tactile fibres worked the same way, what shape would their curve have? What shape would show a preference?
scenes.visual: The myelinated curve stays; a blank dashed space waits for the CT curve. Text: CT curve?
scenes.narration: Predict. If C-tactile fibres worked the same way, what shape would their curve have? What shape would show a preference?

scenes.tts: Their firing traced an inverted U. It was highest for strokes between about one and ten centimetres per second.
scenes.caption: Their firing traced an inverted U. It was highest for strokes between about 1 and 10 cm/s.
scenes.visual: The CT curve draws in as an inverted U on the logarithmic speed axis (ticks 0.3, 3, 30 cm/s evenly spaced), peaking over a shaded band from 1 to 10 cm/s. Label: CT afferents; log axis.
scenes.narration: Their firing traced an inverted U. It was highest for strokes between about 1 and 10 cm/s.

scenes.tts: Slower and faster strokes drove them less.
scenes.visual: Arrows on both slopes of the inverted U point down. Label: the shape, not a higher firing rate, set CT afferents apart.
scenes.narration: Slower and faster strokes drove them less.

scenes.tts: A separate group of volunteers rated the same strokes. Their average pleasantness had the same shape, highest over the same range.
scenes.visual: A second panel: a rating scale beside the brush. The rating curve draws in a second colour, an inverted U over the same 1 to 10 cm/s band. Label: average pleasantness, different volunteers.
scenes.narration: A separate group of volunteers rated the same strokes. Their average pleasantness had the same shape, highest over the same range.

scenes.tts: Of the fibre classes recorded, only the C-tactile afferent had a curve of that shape.
scenes.visual: A line-up of the recorded fibre classes with their curves; only the CT curve lights up as matching the rating curve.
scenes.narration: Of the fibre classes recorded, only the C-tactile afferent had a curve of that shape.

scenes.tts: Why does that matter? Suppose only fibres whose firing rises with speed drove the ratings.
scenes.visual: The rising myelinated curve feeds an arrow labelled read-out into a ratings box.
scenes.narration: Why does that matter? Suppose only fibres whose firing rises with speed drove the ratings.

scenes.tts: If more firing meant more pleasant, ratings would rise with speed. They do not.
scenes.visual: The predicted ratings curve rises; it is crossed out against the real inverted-U ratings.
scenes.narration: If more firing meant more pleasant, ratings would rise with speed. They do not.

scenes.tts: So the caress-tuned fibre is the obvious candidate. But a candidate is a suspect, not a proven cause.
scenes.visual: The CT curve labelled prime suspect, with a question mark beside the word cause.
scenes.narration: So the caress-tuned fibre is the obvious candidate. But a candidate is a suspect, not a proven cause.

scenes.tts: Ratings and recordings came from different people. And other signals combined could, in principle, make the same curve.
scenes.visual: Two silhouettes, one labelled recorded, one labelled rated. Then two rising curves subtract to make an inverted U. Label: in principle.
scenes.narration: Ratings and recordings came from different people. And other signals combined could, in principle, make the same curve.

scenes.tts: The one idea: of the fibres recorded in human hairy skin, the C-tactile afferent fired most at caress speeds.
scenes.visual: Idea card builds line by line: CT afferent, tuned to caress speeds. Small print: recorded fibre classes; soft-brush strokes; group averages.
scenes.narration: The one idea: of the fibres recorded in human hairy skin, the C-tactile afferent fired most at caress speeds.

scenes.tts: Average pleasantness follows its curve. So its input is the prime candidate for the pleasant side of touch.
scenes.visual: Idea card adds: pleasantness follows, so CT input is the prime candidate.
scenes.narration: Average pleasantness follows its curve. So its input is the prime candidate for the pleasant side of touch.

scenes.tts: Only taking the input away can show whether it is needed.
scenes.visual: Idea card completes: only removal can show need. Small arrow to the next chapter: take the input away.
scenes.narration: Only taking the input away can show whether it is needed.
